correctness.rationale: The root-inequality body is the union of a central side-one cube and eight coordinate pyramids of volume 1/8 each, with vertices exactly the eight signed axes and sixteen half-cube corners. It contains the actual Voronoi cell by the root inequalities and has its covolume 2, hence equals it. Strict convexity localizes the endpoint at the vertices, which are transitive under signed permutations and a half-Hadamard matrix (the latter preserves the roots). At e1 the cap coordinates (1−s,su) have Jacobian s³ and squared radius 1−2s+(1+U)s². The small quadratic root cuts off each ray uniformly for small epsilon, giving 24 caps divided by volume 2, i.e. 3∫t⁴. For an independent Taylor check put q=epsilon−epsilon²/2, A=(1+U)/2; t=q+At² so by elementary series substitution t⁴=q⁴+4Aq⁵+14A²q⁶+O(q⁷). The uniform cube moments E[A]=1, E[A²]=16/15 give 24, 48, 772/5 on converting from q. The root has a complex analytic branch uniformly near zero for all U in [0,3]; rational polynomial coefficients integrate to rational numbers. Continuity of the radial law and independence give the stated maximum limit, including t=0. The equal-unit-radius cube has sixteen corner caps, each with leading volume (2 epsilon)^4/4! and hence total coefficient 32/3; the ratio is 9/4 only in the stated common-radius comparison, with volumes 2 and 1. Frozen checker inspected, not executed; the argument is local, not a full radial CDF.
